name: EPA National Walkability Index
gap: US-wide replacement for the NYC-only infrastructure/transit pillar (subway_access, planned_catalysts are NYC MTA-specific and have no fallback outside NYC).
coverage: National (all 50 states + DC + PR per the data.gov catalog description; not independently re-verified this run).
granularity: Census block group (finer than the tract/ZCTA floor this project needs). Does NOT aggregate cleanly to this project's NTAs, though: this vintage is built on 2010-Census block-group geography (per the EPA Smart Location Database), while the project's NTAs are the 2020 vintage (per census_acs.py's docstring) -- the block-group IDs won't nest directly into 2020 NTA codes. A spatial/area-weighted join using the index's shapefile geometries (shapely is already a dependency) would be needed, not a plain code lookup.
update_frequency: Irregular / infrequent. Current vintage is built on 2019 Census block groups; EPA's own catalog metadata was last touched Feb 2025 but the underlying index itself does not appear to have had a newer vintage since. Acceptable for a built-environment metric (walkability/transit proximity changes slowly), not acceptable if treated as a timely signal.
history: No real time series — this is a point-in-time structural index (one vintage), not a growth-rate input. Pairs with transit/density metrics already in the 'infrastructure' pillar rather than the 'momentum' pillar.
license: US government work, public domain. No redistribution restriction found.
cost: Free. No rate limit found — delivered as a one-time bulk ZIP/shapefile download (EPA Smart Location Mapping page) or an ArcGIS REST MapServer endpoint (geodata.epa.gov) for querying without downloading the whole file.

correlation.reason_not_computed: app/research/evaluate_series.py does not exist yet (Phase 4 per the research-sources skill), and wasn't run by hand this run. Note this IS testable once ingested, just not with evaluate_series.py's lead/lag design built for a growth-rate series: as a static level it should instead be tested cross-sectionally against later ZHVI/ZORI growth, the same way backtest.py already tests the valuation-gap level against next-period appreciation (see the Spearman-correlation comment on DEFAULT_WEIGHTS in neighborhood.py). That test hasn't been run -- this is a note on how to evaluate it, not a result.

recommendation: Recommend with caveats. This is the strongest fit found for the stated gap: free, no-login, block-group granularity, and genuinely national -- a real substitute for subway_access/planned_catalysts once the project has non-NYC neighborhoods to score. But it's not an unqualified 'clears every bar' pick: (1) it's a single static snapshot with no refreshable time series, so there's no appreciation-correlation evidence behind it yet -- that would need the cross-sectional backtest described above before leaning on it heavily; (2) its block-group geography is 2010-vintage and won't line up with this project's 2020 NTAs without a spatial join; (3) it's a composite index (density, diversity, design, transit sub-scores bundled into one 1-20 score), so an implementer should decide whether to ingest the composite or the sub-scores separately for consistency with this project's one-MetricDef-per-signal style.
